title: Spiral Matrix
statement: You get a grid with any number of rows and columns. Read its values in a spiral: start at the top-left, go right along the top row, down the right column, left along the bottom row, up the left column, then keep winding inward. Return the values in that order.

example.caption: A 3 by 3 grid read as a spiral. The path ends in the middle.

idea.sentence: Keep four fences (top, bottom, left, right) around the cells not yet read, walk one side at a time, and pull that side's fence inward after each walk.

jargon.plain: My name for a boundary index: top and bottom are row numbers, left and right are column numbers. Cells outside the four fences are already read.
One lap of the outer edge of the still-unread area. After a ring the unread area is a smaller rectangle.

watch.inputHint: One argument: a matrix (list of equal-length rows) with at least one row and one column, like [[1,2],[3,4]].

vars.meaning: number of cells in the matrix (rows times columns)

compare.bruteLabel: Walk with a direction and a visited grid
compare.optimalLabel: Walk four sides between shrinking fences

rows.name: Direction + visited grid
rows.note: Step forward, turn right when you hit an edge or a visited cell. Needs a second grid of flags.

rows.name: Four fences
rows.note: Each cell is read once. Apart from the answer list, only four integers are stored.

fast.takeaway: Every cell must be read, so n is the floor for both. The fences just remove the visited grid and the turn logic.

stages.title: Set the fences
stages.note: top = 0, bottom = last row, left = 0, right = last column. Keep going while top <= bottom and left <= right.

stages.title: Top row
stages.note: Read the top row from left to right, then move the top fence down by one.

stages.title: Right column
stages.note: Read the right column from the new top down to the bottom, then move the right fence left by one.

stages.title: Bottom row
stages.note: Only if a row is left (top <= bottom): read the bottom row right to left, then move the bottom fence up.

stages.title: Left column
stages.note: Only if a column is left (left <= right): read the left column bottom to top, then move the left fence right.

edges.title: One row
edges.why: The top row takes everything and the top fence passes the bottom. Without the row guard the bottom row step would read the same cells backwards.

edges.title: One column
edges.why: The top cell and the right column cover all of it. The right fence then crosses the left one, and the left column guard stops a second pass.

edges.title: Odd by odd
edges.why: The last ring is a single cell. Only the top-row step reads it. The other three sides find nothing left to read.

edges.title: Wide rectangle
edges.why: The rings do not meet in a cell but in a row, so a guard must stop the bottom row after the fences cross.

gotchas.text: Without the two guards (top <= bottom, left <= right) a single row or a single column gets read twice. Re-check after the first two sides, because those moves changed the fences.
Move the fence right after its walk, not at the end of the loop. The next side must start from the new fence.
matrix[0].length throws on an empty matrix. The task promises at least one row and one column. Add a guard if you ever reuse this on raw input.
Start with out := []int{} (not var out []int) if callers may print or JSON-encode the result. A nil slice encodes to null, an empty one to [].
A [][]int has no fixed row width. len(matrix[0]) is the column count only if every row is the same length, which the problem guarantees.

recap.key: Walk top row, right column, bottom row, left column, moving each fence in after its side. Guard the last two sides.
recap.complexity: Time O(rows x columns). Space O(1) besides the output.
moves: Top row then top++; right column then right--
If top <= bottom: bottom row then bottom--
If left <= right: left column then left++
